title: The codec's input noise — 2026-10-13
meta: 2026-10-13 · LIN 1 wired to input board LIN1, input board GND connected to Codec GND. input board V9 connected to 9V battery +, input board GND connected to battery -. input board IN to jack tip. input board GND connected to jack sleeve. 20cm TRS cable plugged into jack, other end connected to guitar, player touching the guitar strings. input board SW-C jumpered to SW-L. U1 pin 3 shorted to board ground.
intro: Three arms, each 20 s of the codec's own ADC — channel 0, LIN1 — analysed from 2 s in, because the stream's start-up transient sits in the first seconds. What the input node is connected to decides what is in them: a pin shorted to ground measures the converter and the wiring to it, an input board measures the board, a jack measures whatever the jack is picking up.

The state line above is the only description of the setup in this record, and it is what the owner typed when the run was started. The script cannot see the wiring and does not know what it measured; the numbers below say how quiet whatever it was, was.
callout: How to read it. Each capture has a spectrum in dBFS per 0.73 Hz bin and the same noise as octave-band bars. Hum is a spike at 50 Hz and its harmonics, and the mains line beside each graph is that spike: an A-weighted figure discounts 50 Hz by about 30 dB, which is why a hum reads far worse unweighted than weighted. Hiss is a broad slope across the high bands. Drift is energy below 20 Hz, which the band-limited figures do not count and the raw one does. The three arms are the converter in its three states — the engine running, a silent playback stream, and neither — so where they disagree the difference is the engine or the stream, and where they agree whatever it is sits ahead of both, in the wiring at the input node.
footer: Captured by scripts/codec-input-noise.py, analysed and drawn by scripts/codec-noise.py and scripts/noise-document.py. The engine and host state around the run is in state.json.

captures.label: Engine running, muted — the pedal's normal state
captures.note: The engine holds the codec and renders its document, muted, which is what the player's audio path carries. Captured through namchainctl record: the engine's own capture path, the one the bench test's “Guitar input noise” uses. 2026-10-11 read −75.3 dBFS(A) here at 64-frame periods.

captures.label: Engine stopped, a silent playback stream open
captures.note: No engine, but a silent aplay holds the playback path open — the codec state the engine leaves it in. On 2026-10-11 this converter's capture-only state was about 15 dB louder in the 4–16 kHz bands and this arm read −79.9 dBFS(A), the quietest of that session's arms — not of every session's since.

captures.label: Engine stopped, capture only (no playback stream)
captures.note: The engine stopped and arecord on its own. The arm the earlier logs quote, and the least repeatable of the three: 2026-10-11 read −75.8 dBFS(A) in the settled re-run, but 4–16 kHz dominated and 15 dB louder with the Pico attached earlier the same day.
